item.title: Jamaat ameer: Another revolution imminent, people must prepare
item.description:
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer and Opposition Leader in Parliament Dr Shafiqur Rahman on Wednesday said that "another revolution" appears to be imminent, calling on the people to prepare for what he described as the next phase of the movement against fascism.
Speaking as the chief guest at a rally organized by the 11-party alliance at the south gate of Baitul Mukarram National Mosque, marking the second anniversary of the July Mass Uprising, Shafiqur alleged that the country was again heading toward a situation that would require public resistance.
Addressing unnamed political opponents, he said that if they had not "betrayed" the people, there would have been no reason for unrest, adding that his party could not remain silent while the country faced its current circumstances.
He said revolutions transcend age, noting that people of all ages had participated in the July Mass Uprising and expressing hope that they would again take part in future movements. He also said the struggle against what he described as fascism would continue.
Shafiqur said threats of imprisonment, repression or execution would not deter his party, adding that, if necessary, they would embrace even the gallows in pursuit of what they believe is the nation's liberation.
Claiming that some political actors who had once been victims of oppression were now repeating the same practices, the Jamaat chief urged them to refrain from what he called fascist behavior. He said that if leaders respected the people, they would, in turn, earn public respect, while vowing that no form of fascism would be tolerated in Bangladesh.
He also urged the government to respect what he described as the people's mandate, claiming that ignoring public opinion had historically led to the downfall of those in power.
Shafiqur further alleged that his party was facing continuous pressure to compromise and being offered various inducements, but said Jamaat would continue to safeguard the people's mandate and would not retreat from its demands under any circumstances.
Referring to recent developments on university campuses, he claimed that students and teachers were living in fear and alleged that the culture of "gonorooms" and "guest rooms" was re-emerging. He called on students, teachers and staff to resist injustice wherever it occurs.
Criticizing the recent increase in gas prices, the Jamaat ameer alleged that authorities first create an artificial gas shortage before raising prices and then resolve the crisis afterward. He described the practice as deception against the public.
The rally was chaired by Bangladesh Khelafat Majlish Ameer Mamunul Haque and was also addressed by other leaders of the 11-party alliance.

item.title: 10 injured in clash between Chhatra Dal, Shibir activists at Barisal University
item.description:
At least 10 people were injured in a clash between activists of Chhatra Dal and Chhatra Shibir at Barisal University on Wednesday over allegations that outsiders had joined a campus rally.
The clash broke out in the morning when the university unit of Chhatra Shibir brought out a procession titled "Indomitable July," according to witnesses and campus sources.
An argument reportedly began after Chhatra Dal activists objected to the alleged presence of outsiders in the rally. The altercation later escalated into a clash, followed by several rounds of chase and counter-chase.
Ashiq Ahmed, senior vice-president of the university unit of Chhatra Dal, alleged that Chhatra Shibir had entered the campus with outsiders carrying sticks and flags.
He claimed that Shibir activists attacked Chhatra Dal members after they requested that the programme be held without outsiders, leaving five to six of their activists injured.
Rejecting the allegation, Zakaria Islam Babu, general secretary of the university unit of Chhatra Shibir, said they had been holding a peaceful program marking the anniversary of the July Uprising when Chhatra Dal activists attacked them near the vice-chancellor's gate.
He claimed that around five Shibir activists were injured in the attack and alleged that the incident occurred in the presence of university authorities. Although the university proctor tried to control the situation, the attack continued, he added.
Zakaria also said a complaint had been submitted to the university's vice-chancellor seeking justice over the incident.
Both student organisations blamed each other for triggering the violence.
The university proctor could not be reached for comment.
Belal Hossain, additional deputy commissioner of Barisal Metropolitan Police, said police rushed to the campus after receiving information about the clash.
"Additional police have been deployed on the campus following the incident. We have urged both sides to remain calm," he said.
Earlier on Tuesday, violence erupted as activists of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) and Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir clashed at several educational institutions in the capital, leaving dozens injured.

item.title: State July celebration disrupted over documentary controversy
item.description:
A state ceremony marking the second anniversary of the July Mass Uprising descended into protests on Wednesday after audience members accused the government of distorting the movement’s history through an official documentary, forcing ministers to apologise and promise immediate corrections.
The unprecedented disruption unfolded in the presence of Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmed Bir Bikram at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Center, where families of July martyrs, injured protesters, students and political activists interrupted the program with chants of “Fake, fake” after the documentary was screened.
The protest briefly threw the nationally televised event into disorder, prompting members of the acting president’s security detail to take positions on the stage and inside the auditorium while several invited foreign guests left the venue amid the commotion.
The controversy centred on allegations that the documentary failed to accurately portray the July uprising, omitted key developments -- particularly the events of August 3 -- and inadequately reflected the sacrifices of protesters and the movement’s leadership.
As slogans echoed through the auditorium, organisers repeatedly appealed for calm, but the protest continued.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed eventually addressed the gathering, inviting protesters to speak from the stage and urging them to remain seated.
Seeking to defuse tensions, he requested National Citizen Party (NCP) Member Secretary Akhtar Hossain to address the audience.
Akhtar acknowledged the concerns raised by protesters, saying the documentary contained “inconsistencies” that required correction.
“We have also seen the inconsistencies in the documentary,” he said.
“The events of August 3 are completely absent. We will raise these issues with the government and seek accountability from the ministry. But on this historic day, we must remain calm out of respect for the families of the martyrs.”
Following his appeal, Akhtar and other NCP leaders left the venue after taking permission from the acting president.
As protests continued, Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Aazam Khan returned to the stage and publicly apologised to the audience.
“Today’s documentary has caused you pain,” he said.
“The July movement and the mass uprising belong to all of us. We will carefully review every inconsistency, including the omission of the events of August 3, and take immediate steps to correct them.”
He also assured the audience that the documentary would be reviewed in consultation with representatives of the martyrs’ families and injured July fighters before being revised.
Only after the minister’s apology and commitment to amend the film did the protesters withdraw their objections, allowing the remainder of the program to proceed.
The event, organised by the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs, began with a reception for the families of July martyrs and injured July fighters before the documentary was shown.

item.title: Swapon calls for equitable, accountable state inspired by July Uprising
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon on Wednesday called on all to work together to build an equitable, accountable and humane state inspired by the spirit of the July Mass Uprising.
Speaking at a discussion and reception for families of the July martyrs at the District Shilpakala Academy auditorium in Barishal, organized to mark July Mass Uprising Day 2026, the minister said the ideals of the historic movement must remain alive in the hearts of every citizen.
He said the spirit forged through the sacrifices and aspirations of thousands of people must not be undermined by any force, urging everyone to remain united and vigilant.
Swapon said that a group and a single family had monopolised democracy and people's rights for years, weakening democratic institutions and depriving citizens of their voting rights.
He urged people from all walks of life, regardless of political affiliation, religion or ethnicity, to forge unity to protect democracy.
The minister said attempts had been made to divide people through intimidation, greed and promises of power, but conscious citizens rejected such temptations and prioritised the country's interests.
He emphasized that the July Mass Uprising was not the work of a few individuals but a collective resistance against prolonged deprivation, injustice and oppression.
The strength of this movement is laying in the unity, courage and unwavering faith of the people in democracy, he said.
Barisal Divisional Commissioner Khalil Ahmed chaired the program, where government officials, political leaders, media representatives and families of the July martyrs were present.
A documentary on the July martyrs was also screened.

item.title: 5 protein-rich seeds to add to your diet
item.description:
Protein plays a vital role in building and repairing muscles, producing hormones and enzymes, healing tissues, and supporting healthy skin, hair, and blood. While meat, fish, eggs, and dairy are well-known protein sources, several seeds also provide a significant amount of plant-based protein, along with fiber, healthy fats, vitamins, and minerals.
Here are five protein-rich seeds worth adding to your diet:
Pumpkin seeds
Pumpkin seeds are among the richest plant-based sources of protein. A 28-gram serving (about one ounce) provides around 7 grams of protein. They are also rich in fiber, magnesium, zinc, and essential amino acids, including tryptophan, making them a nutritious snack or salad topping.
Chia seeds
Just two tablespoons of chia seeds provide about 5 grams of protein. They also contain fiber, omega-3 fatty acids, and essential amino acids that support muscle recovery and tissue repair. Their combination of protein, fiber, and healthy fats may help promote fullness, support healthy weight management, and maintain steady blood sugar levels. Chia seeds are also a good source of calcium and phosphorus, which help support bone health.
Flaxseeds
Two tablespoons of flaxseeds contain approximately 5-6 grams of protein. They are also rich in fiber and plant-based omega-3 fatty acids. Regular consumption may help support heart health, improve digestion, and contribute to healthy cholesterol levels as part of a balanced diet.
Sunflower seeds
A 28-gram serving of sunflower seeds provides about 6 grams of protein. They are also an excellent source of vitamin E, magnesium, and selenium. Their protein and amino acid content supports muscle maintenance and tissue repair, making them a nutritious post-workout snack.
Sesame seeds
Three tablespoons of sesame seeds contain roughly 5 grams of protein. They provide essential amino acids, including methionine, which plays a role in protein synthesis and tissue repair. Rich in calcium, magnesium, and phosphorus, sesame seeds also help support bone health and overall nutrition.

item.title: Sand-laden trucks outside Khaleda Zia's residence: Ex-joint secretary sent to jail
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Wednesday sent former joint secretary Syed Jaglul Pasha to jail in a case over allegations that he helped obstruct former prime minister Khaleda Zia from attending a political rally in 2013 by barricading the road outside her Gulshan residence with sand-laden trucks and using pepper spray.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Kamal Uddin passed the order after Gulshan Zonal Team Inspector Anwar Hossain produced Jaglul Pasha before the court and sought a 10-day remand. The court fixed Thursday for the remand hearing. SI Mokhtar Hossain of the prosecution confirmed the matter
Jaglul was arrested by the Dhaka Metropolitan Police's Detective Branch (DB) from his Bashundhara residence at around 1:30am on Tuesday.
According to the case statement, Jaglul was among 111 named accused, along with 250-300 unidentified individuals, who allegedly gathered outside Khaleda Zia's Gulshan residence on December 28, 2013, armed with deadly weapons. They allegedly remained there throughout the day, assaulted BNP leaders and activists, carried out acts of sabotage by blocking roads, and created obstacles to prevent Khaleda Zia from attending a scheduled political rally.
The complaint further alleged that at around 9am on December 29, 2013, when Khaleda Zia was preparing to leave for the rally with her entourage, the accused barricaded the road with sand-laden trucks and other vehicles. Despite repeated attempts to leave, they allegedly prevented her movement and used banned pepper spray with the intent to kill, leaving Khaleda Zia and several leaders and activists accompanying her injured.
The case was filed at Gulshan Police Station in October 2024 by Shariful Islam Shawon, former joint secretary of the Latif Hall unit of Rajshahi University Chhatra Dal.
Jaglul Pasha also faces allegations in the Zia Orphanage Trust case of preparing forged documents and giving false testimony before the court in proceedings involving former prime minister Khaleda Zia.

item.title: Three everyday kitchen items that could be harming your health
item.description:
Some everyday kitchen items—including old sponges, damaged non-stick pans, and dishwashing liquids with harsh chemicals—can pose hidden health risks if they are not used or replaced properly. Experts say simple changes in your kitchen routine can help reduce the risk of foodborne illness and unnecessary chemical exposure.
Old kitchen sponge
Kitchen sponges stay damp for long periods, making them an ideal breeding ground for bacteria and fungi. Over time, they can harbor harmful bacteria such as Salmonella and E. coli . These microbes can contaminate dishes and food, increasing the risk of foodborne illness, including diarrhea, vomiting, stomach infections, and fever.
When to replace it:
Dishwashing liquid with harsh chemicals
Some dishwashing liquids contain artificial fragrances, dyes, and other chemicals that may cause irritation in sensitive individuals. If dishes are not rinsed thoroughly, small amounts of residue may remain on the surface. In some people, this may contribute to skin irritation, dermatitis, eye irritation, or respiratory discomfort.
How to use it safely:
Damaged non-stick pan
A non-stick pan with deep scratches or a peeling coating should be replaced. Tiny particles from the damaged coating may end up in food, while overheating worn non-stick cookware can release fumes that may irritate the eyes and throat and cause temporary flu-like symptoms known as polymer fume fever.
Experts also recommend avoiding overheating non-stick cookware and considering alternatives such as stainless steel, cast iron, or tri-ply cookware.
Safe cookware practices:
Small changes can make a big difference
These kitchen items are not inherently dangerous, but improper use or failure to replace them regularly can increase health risks. Simple habits—such as replacing your sponge regularly, choosing gentler cleaning products, and discarding damaged cookware—can help reduce the risk of foodborne illness and unnecessary exposure to potentially harmful substances.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 854 as five die in 24 hours
item.description:
Five more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Wednesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 854.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all five of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 758, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 96, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the five new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with three deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 959 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Wednesday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 132,905.
During the same period, 124 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 16,655.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 115,234 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 111,005 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.description:
Health officials on Wednesday said they recorded 195 fresh cases of dengue onslaughts in the past 24 hours.
“During the period, (of the 195) 15 patients were hospitalized in Barisal division, 77 in Chittagong division, 21 in Dhaka division, 34 in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and 26 in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) areas, 10 in Khulna division and 12 in Rangpur division, a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) statement said.
Since the start of the dengue onslaughts, Bangladesh this year has witnessed so far 59 deaths while the disease inflicted 17,409.
Last year, dengue claimed 413 lives and inflicted 1,02,861 people in the country.
Besides, dengue claimed 575 lives and inflicted 1,01,214 people in 2024.

item.title: Rubaiyat Hossain's ‘The Difficult Bride’ selected for 51st Toronto Film Festival
item.description:
National Film Award-winning filmmaker Rubaiyat Hossain's latest feature, The Difficult Bride, has been selected for the 51st Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF), marking another international milestone after becoming the first Bangladeshi feature film chosen for the Orizzonti section of the 83rd Venice International Film Festival.
Rubaiyat shared the news on social media, writing: "Next stop TIFF! See you there!" alongside the film's screening schedule.
The Difficult Bride will be screened three times during the festival. The first screening is scheduled for 4pm on September 16, followed by a second screening at 10pm on September 17. The final screening will take place at 12:15pm on September 19.
The first two screenings will be held at TIFF Lightbox Cinema 4 (Paul & Leah Atkinson Family Cinema), while the third will take place at Scotiabank Theatre, Cinema 7.
Set in contemporary Dhaka, The Difficult Bride is a psychological horror film that explores themes of beauty, womanhood, marriage, and societal expectations through a supernatural narrative.
The film stars newcomer Zaineen Chowdhury Karim in the lead role alongside Azmeri Haque Badhan, Reekita Nondine Shimu, Sunerah Binte Kamal, Shatabdi Wadud, Saberi Alam, and Mohammed Bari.
The 51st Toronto International Film Festival will be be held from September 10 to 20.

item.title: Experts stress need to match technical skills with new demands, outline steps taken
Controversy over documentary at July event sparks, NCP leaders walk out
item.description:
A chaosn broke out at an event organised by the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs to mark the second anniversary of the July Mass Uprising.

The programme, titled "Reception for the Families of the July Mass Uprising Martyrs and the July Fighters," was held on Wednesday at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in Agargaon, Dhaka, where Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmad attended as the chief guest.

Leaders of the National Citizen Party (NCP) alleged that a documentary screened at the event did not properly present the chronology of the July Movement. An argument ensued over the issue, after which the NCP leaders left the venue. At one stage during the commotion, diplomats were also seen leaving the venue.

The incident has triggered widespread discussion on social media.

What triggered it

Several videos of the commotion at the programme have already spread on social media. A video shows some of the guests present at the event protesting over the documentary's portrayal of the One-Point demand and matters related to the Nine-Point demands.

Mahin Sarkar, joint member secretary of the National Citizen Party (NCP) and a former coordinator of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement, was present at the function.

Writing on Facebook, he said that the documentary portrayed Prime Minister Tarique Rahman as the announcer of the One-Point demand.

"Nahid Islam (NCP convener), who signed his own death warrant by announcing the One-Point demand, does not exist in the BNP's version of history. Asif Mahmud (NCP spokesperson), who announced the 'Long March to Dhaka' despite knowing death was certain, does not exist in that history either."

Mahin Sarkar further wrote that because he protested against the documentary shown at the programme, the prime minister's forces pounced on him. He said he was assaulted in front of the president.

Meanwhile, videos show that amid the commotion, the programme's moderator repeatedly appealed from the stage for everyone to remain calm. However, the commotion continued.

At that stage, Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Azam Khan went onto the stage. He said, "I request everyone to remain calm." At the same time, he said that if there were any mistakes in the documentary, they would be corrected.

Even then, the audience continued chanting slogans such as, "Stop toying with us." The minister was also seen repeatedly appealing to them.

As order still could not be restored at the programme, State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraq Hossain came to the microphone. In a somewhat scolding tone, he said, "Have you come here to draw attention to yourselves?"

Addressing those chanting slogans, Ishraq Hossain further said, "What are you doing? What have you done for the families of the martyrs? You have done nothing."

After this, Ahmed Azam Khan tried to calm Ishraq Hossain, while at the same time Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed came to the microphone.

The Home Minister said, "Those of you who wish to speak, please come here and speak. ... Say what you have to say; we will listen. But please sit down calmly."

NCP walks out of the venue

While speaking, the Home Minister called Akhter Hossen, member secretary of the National Citizen Party (NCP), several times.

After a while, Akhter Hossen came onto the stage. He said, "As one of the July fighters and as a representative of my party, I wish this programme every success. But, personally, and on behalf of my fellow fighters who are with me, in our aspiration for something better, it is not possible for me to remain at this programme."

Akhtar further said, "I thank the honourable President at today's programme. We embrace the way he has stood for Bangladesh. He is both a freedom fighter and a July fighter, and I express my respect to him. With that respect, I have decided to quietly leave this venue."

Before leaving the stage, the NCP member secretary said, "Even at a state programme, we have failed to embrace the entirety of our history. You will notice that, just as the Awami League once monopolised the history of the Liberation War in Bangladesh in a one-sided manner, a similar situation has been created here."

Akhter Hossen alleged that the documentary produced by the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs made no mention of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement or the Nine-Point demands. It also omitted the announcement of the One-Point demand made at the Central Shaheed Minar on 3 August 2024.

'I am deeply saddened,' says Acting President

Expressing anger over the disorder at the programme, Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmad said that mistakes can happen to anyone. Everyone must work together to correct those mistakes. However, he said he was deeply saddened and distressed by the situation that had unfolded before foreign guests at a national event.

Referring to the incident, Hafiz Uddin Ahmad said, "The way we have been humiliated before foreigners, before our foreign guests, has deeply saddened me. And the person who will be happiest about this incident is the one sitting in the neighbouring country. For that person, today is a day of great joy."

Criticising the mistakes in the documentary shown at the programme, the Acting President said that it did not include a photograph of Abu Sayed. Yet, Abu Sayed is the image and symbol of the July Revolution. Without his photograph, no documentary on that movement can be complete.

The Acting President also noted that the documentary did not include a photograph of BNP Chairperson Begum Khaleda Zia.

Earlier, in his speech, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said that the July Mass Uprising must not be "appropriated by any political party." He said, "If we keep asking, 'Whose July is it? Whose July is it?' then July will belong to none of us. We must free ourselves from this situation."

item.title: Tourist dies at five-star hotel swimming pool in Cox's Bazar
item.description:
A tourist has died after entering the swimming pool of a five-star hotel in the Marine Drive area of Ukhiya, Cox's Bazar.

The incident occurred yesterday, Tuesday afternoon, the hotel Baywatch on Inani Beach in the upazila.

The tourist had entered the pool with his family members. Police suspect that he died of a heart attack.

The deceased tourist was Miraj Ahmed (38), who was from Munshiganj.

Witnesses said that he became unconscious after entering the swimming pool. The hotel authorities later rescued him and took him to Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital, where physicians declared him dead.

According to the hotel authorities, Miraj Ahmed had travelled from Munshiganj to Cox's Bazar on Monday with his wife and children for a two-day trip.

They then checked into the Baywatch Hotel in Inani. At around 3:00 pm yesterday, he entered the swimming pool with his family members.

However, after a while, he became unconscious. He was rescued and taken to Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital, where physicians declared him dead.

Md Atikur Rahman Majumder, officer-in-charge (OC) of Ukhiya Police Station, told Prothom Alo that Miraj Ahmed lost consciousness after suffering cardiac arrest while swimming in the pool.

After speaking with the family members, police learned that Miraj Ahmed had been suffering from heart disease. An unnatural death case has been filed with Ukhiya Police Station in connection with the incident.

Following an application by the family, the body was handed over to them today without an autopsy, he added.

item.title: Family alleges premeditated murder, police investigating multiple possible motives
item.description:
A case has been filed in connection with the recovery of the bodies of a young man and his mother and grandmother from a residence in Kachua, Bagerhat.

On Wednesday, the family filed a murder case with the police, listing unknown suspects.

The three deceased are Ahad Hawladar (25), son of the late Abdar Ali Hawladar of Chandarkola village, Radipara Union, Kachua Upazila; his mother Monira Begum (60); and grandmother Rashida Begum (93).

Rashida Begum was the wife of the late Abdur Rashid of Brishtipur village in Bagerhat Sadar Upazila.

On Tuesday afternoon, locals found the three bodies lying in their residence in Chandarkola village and informed the police. The autopsy of the deceased was completed today at the Bagerhat District Hospital morgue.

Relatives allege that they were murdered in a planned manner. Money and gold jewelry have gone missing from the residence. Blood was found on various pieces of furniture, the bed, the mosquito net, and the mud floor inside the house.

In connection with the incident, Monira Begum's elder son Faisal Hawladar has filed a case.

The police have not yet been able to confirm the motive or method behind the murders. Investigation agencies are working to uncover the mystery, keeping various possibilities in mind.

Although the bodies were recovered on Tuesday, the murders may have happened at least two days earlier. Based on the injury marks, law enforcement believes that tools like hammers and crowbars (shabols) were used in the murders. Marks of strangulation were also observed.

Regarding this, the Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Kachua Police Station, Mahamud Hasan, said that the police are trying to identify and arrest those involved. An investigation has begun to uncover the mystery of the murders, considering multiple possible causes.

Mahamud Hasan mentioned that following the autopsies, the bodies have been handed over to the family.

Rashida Begum's body was buried at her home in Brishtipur, Sadar Upazila, in the afternoon. The bodies of the mother and son will be buried in the family graveyard in front of their house.

The deceased, Ahad Hawladar, was the youngest of three siblings. He was an electrician by profession. His middle brother, Faisal Hawladar, worked in Dhaka, and his elder sister, Ramisha Khatun, is a housewife.

Faisal said, "Our grandmother (Rashida Begum) came to visit us a few days ago. Last Sunday, I spoke to my mother on the phone. It was around 7-8 PM. I spoke with my brother that day too. After that, no one from the house communicated. On Monday, I couldn’t get anyone on the phone.

A woman from the neighboring house said, ''The fan is on in your house, I’m calling your mother, but there's no response. I tried calling, but the phone was off.'' I thought they all went to our grandmother's house. Yesterday, a cousin called to say grandmother had passed away. ”

Faisal further added, "We had no enemies. My mother's dream was to build a house. Whatever my younger brother and I earned, we gave it all to mother. Half of the house was already built. Only the roof was left. The money for the roof was also with her. "

item.title: 'Where did police dispose of the body?' Family still searching for Hridoy, shot on 5 August
item.description:
It was 3:25 pm on 5 August 2024. Following the news that Sheikh Hasina had fled the country, jubilant crowds gathered in the area adjacent to Sharif General Hospital on Kashimpur Road in Konabari, Gazipur. Konabari Police Station is nearby. Thousands of people brought out victory processions along the road. Noon passed into the afternoon. The procession and celebrations were still on.

It was 5:22 pm. Several police members wearing riot police uniforms detained a young man. They surrounded the young man and took him onto the road in front of Sharif General Hospital. Several more police members came there and gathered around. One police member was holding a shotgun.

He went and stood behind the young man. Suddenly, one police member in the group slapped the young man. Then the police member standing behind him with the shotgun shot the young man. The sound of a gunshot, followed by a puff of smoke. The young man collapsed to the ground with his arms and legs outstretched. His body was still moving slightly. Leaving the bullet-hit young man there, the police members walked away.

The police member who had fired the shot looked back once at the bullet-hit young man before leaving. A few more police members then came there and carried the young man away by his hands and feet. A few minutes later, four police members were seen taking the young man past the front of the hospital. A trail of blood on the road was still clearly visible.

The young man's hands and feet were still moving slightly. Dragging him along, they took him past the hospital towards another group of police members. There were three people in that group—two in uniform and one in plain clothes. They took the bullet-hit young man towards an alley. The alley led straight to Konabari Police Station. At that time, the sound of gunfire was heard again. Leaving the bullet-hit young man at the entrance to the alley, the three men walked away. They later returned, dragged the young man along the ground, and disappeared into the alley with him.

This is not a scene from a work of fiction. It is a scene from a documentary. It depicts the final few tragic moments of a young man's life. The documentary was produced by the International Truth and Justice Project (ITJP), an international human rights organisation, after verifying various pieces of footage recorded on mobile phones and collected from social media, and conducting a forensic analysis of them. The Tech Global Institute provided assistance. The documentary was produced and directed by The Outsider Movie Company.

The name of the young victim was Md Hridoy (21). Hridoy, the only son of Lal Mia and Rehena Begum of Alamnagar village in Gopalpur upazila of Tangail, had two sisters. He lived in the Konabari area. He was a Class XII student at Hemnagar Degree College in Tangail. At the same time, he drove an autorickshaw. On 5 August 2024, after hearing the news that then prime minister Sheikh Hasina had fled, Hridoy left his home.

No trace of Hridoy

On the alley leading towards Konabari Police Station stands Abed Ali Market, lined with a row of shuttered shops. Hridoy was dragged through this very alley. After that, the researchers and makers of the documentary found no footage showing what happened to him. Months have passed, a year has gone by—yet the family has still found no trace of Hridoy.

For two years, the family has been searching desperately for him. The family members no longer even hold on to the hope of getting their loved one back. Speaking to Prothom Alo over the phone on Saturday, 1 August, Hridoy's sister Jesmin Akter said, "We never got my brother back. We searched for his body in the river once, but couldn't find it. After that, nothing happened."

Expressing her anguish, Jesmin said, "My brother's name isn't in the gazette. His name isn't on the list of martyrs either. We haven't received any government assistance. Jamaat-e-Islami has provided help at different times. A student from Dhaka came and gave my father an autorickshaw."

Now, the family says it would find at least some solace if they could recover Hridoy's remains and bury them. Jesmin said, "They took my brother somewhere. We never got my brother back."

Hridoy's father, Lal Mia, submitted an application to the Tangail Deputy Commissioner's office in 2024. In it, he sought the recovery of his son's remains and demanded state recognition. On 21 October 2024, Hridoy's sister, Jesmin, filed a complaint with the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) over Hridoy's disappearance after being shot. Jesmin said, "It would be enough if we could at least find my brother's bones. I want those who killed my brother to be hanged."

What happened that day

On 26 August 2024, Md Ibrahim, brother-in-law of Hridoy, filed a case with Konabari Police Station. The case alleged that police shot Hridoy and disposed of his body. Both Hridoy and Ibrahim drove autorickshaws in Konabari. On the afternoon of 5 August 2024, they had left home together.

Recalling the events, Ibrahim said that after the news spread that Sheikh Hasina had fled, a procession came out, and the police charged at it and fired tear gas. He then told Hridoy to return home. Later, he himself took shelter in a house near the police station. In the afternoon, a female tenant of that house came and said, "The police have shot a man. I wonder which mother's heart has been left empty."

After hearing this, Ibrahim called Hridoy's mobile phone. An unfamiliar person answered. He said that he had found the mobile phone lying on the road. Later, that person met Ibrahim and handed over Hridoy's mobile phone.

Ibrahim said that her wife Jesmin was at home at the time. He called Jesmin and told her to quickly look for her brother. Jesmin then called Hridoy's mobile phone. She, too, heard the voice of an unfamiliar person answering. Earlier that afternoon, Jesmin had had her last conversation with Hridoy. Hridoy had told his sister that his mobile phone balance had run out and that he would recharge it and call her at night. That conversation between the brother and sister never took place.

Ibrahim sets out in search

Amid the gunfire and tension, Ibrahim courageously set out to search for his brother-in-law, Hridoy. Near the place where Hridoy had been shot, he saw a blue lungi lying on the ground and picked it up. Ibrahim said it was Hridoy's lungi. The documentary shows the bullet-hit young man wearing a pair of red shorts. According to Ibrahim, Hridoy had been wearing the red shorts underneath the lungi. During the dragging, the lungi he was wearing may have come off and fallen onto the road. Ibrahim later picked it up from there.

That night, Ibrahim searched for Hridoy's body at Konabari Police Station and at the morgues of nearby hospitals. Later, he also went to the morgue of Dhaka Medical College Hospital. Suddenly, news came that a body stuffed inside a sack had been found in Tongi. Ibrahim rushed there as well. But the body was not Hridoy's. Ibrahim said, "Who knows where the police disposed of the body."

After the evening of 5 August, the police at Konabari Police Station fled. For the next few days, all that remained of the police station were its chairs, tables and building. So Ibrahim could neither go to the police station to look for Hridoy nor file a complaint at that time.

'I will bury my son. Even his bones will be enough'

On 29 January 2025, Prothom Alo published a video report on Hridoy titled, "I want my son's body. Even if it is only his bones, I will bring him home." In the video, Hridoy's father, Lal Mia, who drives a van, said, "He was my only son. What more can I say? I just want to get his body. I will bury my son. Even if I get only his bones, that will be enough."

The day after the incident (6 August 2024), Hridoy was supposed to return to his home in Tangail. His sister Jesmin said that when Hridoy last left home for Konabari, he was in such a hurry that he did not eat the rice that had been served to him. Their mother, Rehena Begum, still lives with that regret.

Speaking to Prothom Alo over the phone, Jesmin said, "From the video footage that has been found, there is no way to hope that my brother is still alive. When the police attack began that afternoon, Hridoy had taken shelter in a shop. Later, the police dragged Hridoy away from in front of a garage there."

The narration of the documentary on Hridoy says that he was killed after being shot from behind with the barrel of a shotgun pressed against his body. On 15 January last year, the documentary was screened at an event at Bangla Academy in the capital. It was also shown by various media outlets. As a result, Hridoy's case once again came into public discussion.

Searching for the body in the Turag

On 24 July 2025, police launched an extensive search operation to recover Hridoy's body. Led by the investigation team of the ICT, the operation was carried out in the Turag River in the Kodda area of Gazipur City, with diver teams from Gazipur, Tongi and Dhaka taking part. Nothing was found.

The police member seen in the video footage shooting Hridoy is Md Akram Hossain. Following the confessional statement given by Constable Akram after his arrest, the operation to search for Hridoy's body was conducted in the Turag River.

On 13 October last year, the then Chief Prosecutor of the ICT, Mohammad Tajul Islam, told the tribunal that Hridoy's body had been dumped in the Kodda River after he had been shot dead. The tribunal had fixed 12 July as the date for submitting the investigation report. The report has not yet been submitted.

Jesmin said that in July this year, they were called to Dhaka. They were informed that those who had killed Hridoy had been arrested. However, those who had dragged Hridoy away by holding his hands and feet have still not been arrested. They were also told that the investigation report would be submitted to the tribunal soon. Since then, they have received no further update on the progress. So the family's wait continues.

item.title: Home Minister: Every letter of July Charter will be implemented
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Wednesday pledged that the government would implement every letter of the July National Charter, while urging all political parties and citizens to remain united against fascism and avoid divisions over the legacy of the July Mass Uprising.
"The July National Charter will be implemented in every letter and spirit," he said.
He was speaking at a reception and discussion for the families of July martyrs and July fighters, organized by the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Center in the capital.
The minister said the aspirations of the July Mass Uprising could only be fulfilled through national unity and constitutional reforms.
Ahmed added that political parties should work together to realize the people's mandate through constitutional amendments and institutional reforms.
He warned against attempts to claim exclusive ownership of the July Uprising, saying it was the collective achievement of the people of Bangladesh, built on years of sacrifice, enforced disappearances, killings, political repression and democratic struggles.
"If, after freeing ourselves from dictatorship, we continue asking who owns July, then July will belong to none of us," he said, urging all democratic forces to remain united to ensure that fascism never returns to Bangladesh.
The minister said reforms would ultimately require constitutional amendments to institutionalize the ideals of the July Mass Uprising and establish a democratic framework capable of preventing future authoritarian rule.
Referring to enforced disappearances, Ahmed said the government was preparing legislation to prevent such crimes and provide justice for victims, expressing hope that the proposed law would be placed before parliament.
On the issue of the Awami League, activities of which are currently banned, he said political parties, like individuals, could face trial for crimes against humanity if warranted by law, but maintained that any decision regarding the party's future should come through the judiciary rather than executive action.
Calling the July Mass Uprising a historic national achievement, the minister urged all political forces to uphold its ideals through unity, democratic reforms and the full implementation of the July Charter.

item.title: Amit: Political parties must show patience and tolerance to fulfil July aspirations

"To fulfil the aspirations of July, every political party must act with patience and tolerance," he said. "If we use the same rhetoric that the fascists once used, it would show that we have not truly embraced democracy. Political ideologies may differ, but at the end of the day, our shared goal is to build a modern, self-reliant Bangladesh."

item.title: DU inaugurates foundation of July Memorial Monument
item.description:
Dhaka University on Wednesday inaugurated the foundation of the July Memorial Monument, which is being built in memory of those killed during the July 2024 mass uprising.
Dhaka University Vice-Chancellor Prof ABM Obaidul Islam inaugurated the project at a ceremony held on the campus.
Among those present were the fathers of martyrs Mir Mughdo, Faiyaz and Yamin, along with the university's Pro-Vice-Chancellors (Academic and Administration), Treasurer, deans of different faculties, the proctor, teachers and university officials.
Speaking at the programme, the vice-chancellor said: "Two years ago today, a new sun rose over Bangladesh through the mass uprising that began on July 1 and culminated on what protesters referred to as '36 July,' or August 5. Sheikh Hasina fled the country with her sister. We have achieved a new Bangladesh through the blood of the martyrs."
He paid tribute to those killed and injured during the uprising and prayed for the eternal peace of the departed souls.
"To preserve the memory of the martyrs of the uprising, we are establishing the July Memorial Monument," he said.
Prof Obaidul alleged that, over the past 17 years, the Awami League government had committed various injustices to consolidate its power while ignoring the will and demands of the people.
"We cannot measure the extent to which people were indiscriminately killed and shot in their own country. There can be no forgiveness for such acts," he said.
The vice-chancellor also said the university had not forgotten what he described as the suppression of dissent under the previous Dhaka University administration.
"We have not forgotten the persecution of dissenting voices," he said, expressing hope that "fascism will never return to this country on the blood of the martyrs."

item.title: Ziaur Rahman killing case: Prosecution seeks Facebook data of Mozaffar
item.description:
The prosecution has written to Meta seeking the Facebook and Messenger data of former army officer Md Mozaffar Hossain, who was arrested over allegations of involvement in the killing of late president Ziaur Rahman.
International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Prosecutor and IT expert Tanvir Hasan Zoha confirmed the matter to Dhaka Tribune on Wednesday.
According to the prosecution, the request was made after investigators found evidence that Mozaffar had communicated directly with several individuals through Messenger and maintained contact with certain groups. Efforts are also underway to recover his deleted Messenger conversations.
Zoha said the information has been sought to assist the tribunal's ongoing investigation into crimes against humanity.
The prosecution has requested subscriber information, account registration details, all current and previously registered email addresses and phone numbers, complete login history with timestamps, IP addresses and devices used to access the account, browser information, and all Facebook Messenger data, including deleted conversations.
Ziaur Rahman, founder of the BNP and the country's then president, was killed during a military uprising in Chittagong on May 30, 1981.
Investigators allege that former army officer Mozaffar Hossain played a role in the disappearance of Ziaur Rahman's body after the killing. At the time, he held the rank of major in the Bangladesh Army. He went into hiding following the incident, and authorities announced a reward for information leading to his arrest.
After remaining a fugitive for 45 years, he was arrested by Detective Branch (DB) police from Banani in Dhaka on the night of July 15 and was subsequently handed over to the Bangladesh Army.
On July 23, ICT-2 ordered that Mozaffar be shown arrested in a crimes against humanity case linked to the July Mass Uprising. The tribunal also granted investigators two days to interrogate him and directed that he remain in army custody.
Earlier, ICT Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam said investigators had found evidence of regular communication between Mozaffar and retired lieutenant general Masud Uddin Chowdhury.
According to the chief prosecutor, Masud was one of the influential figures in the army-backed caretaker government in 2007 and is currently in custody in a crimes against humanity case. Mozaffar has also been shown arrested in the same case.
Aminul Islam said Mozaffar's trial over the killing of Ziaur Rahman would proceed under military law and is separate from the ICT proceedings.
"Our investigation concerns crimes against humanity. We will examine whether he had any involvement during the Awami League government's 16 years in power. Our judicial process is completely separate," he said.
He added that Mozaffar would remain in army custody and be brought before ICT investigators for questioning whenever necessary. If the allegations are established, he will face trial under the tribunal's applicable laws.

item.title: Suspected measles death toll continues to rise
item.description:
Although no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the past 24 hours, the country continues to record a steady rise in suspected measles deaths. During the 24 hours until Wednesday morning, five more children died with suspected measles, while another 1,083 children were either infected with measles or developed measles-like symptoms.
Public health experts said that although confirmed measles deaths have declined, the continued occurrence of suspected deaths suggests the outbreak is still not fully under control.
They attributed the large-scale outbreak to gaps in vaccination coverage, disruptions to the routine immunization programme and low vaccine uptake in some areas.
According to the latest Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) data, a total of 854 children died from confirmed or suspected measles between March 15 and 8am on August 5. Of them, 758 died from suspected measles and 96 from laboratory-confirmed measles.
During the same period, suspected measles cases reached 129,905, while confirmed cases stood at 16,655.
An analysis of DGHS data shows that from the start of the outbreak until July 31, a total of 837 children died from measles or measles-like illness, averaging nearly six deaths a day. During the same period, 128,310 patients were hospitalized, an average of 923 admissions daily.
During the first 30 days of the outbreak, until April 14, 198 children died and 19,361 patients were hospitalized.
By May 14, the death toll had risen to 439, while hospital admissions reached 54,419.
By June 13, deaths had increased to 648 and hospital admissions stood at 84,899.
By July 13, the total death toll had reached 759, while 112,376 patients had been hospitalized.
As of August 5, the total death toll had climbed to 854, while total infections had reached 146,560.
The data show that the daily death rate has not declined significantly since the early stages of the outbreak. Even after the nationwide vaccination campaign ended, hospitals continue to admit more than 900 new patients a day on average.
Senior physician Professor Dr ABM Abdullah said recent disruptions to routine immunization have created a major public health risk.
"We did not see measles deaths 20 to 30 years ago. Although measles is a serious disease, it is easily preventable. The current situation has arisen because many children did not receive vaccines on time. Malnutrition and a lack of breastfeeding are also contributing factors," he said.
He said the government had already completed a nationwide Measles-Rubella (MR) vaccination campaign, while research by icddr,b found no problems with the vaccine's effectiveness. However, it takes one to two months after vaccination for the body to develop immunity.
"That period has already passed, but infections are not declining at the expected rate. Adults are now also becoming infected with measles," he said, adding that those who have not yet been vaccinated should be brought under vaccination as quickly as possible.
Public health and vaccination expert Tajul Islam Bari said there is no separate disease known as "suspected measles."
"Patients whose infection is confirmed through laboratory testing are counted as confirmed measles cases if they die. However, because of shortages of testing kits and other limitations, it is not possible to test every patient. As a result, deaths of patients whose symptoms are consistent with measles are recorded as suspected measles deaths," he said.
He said many children are admitted to hospital with pneumonia, while the initial symptoms of measles include fever, a cold, cough and a sore throat, followed later by a rash. Pneumonia can also develop as a complication of measles.
He said infected children should receive treatment as quickly as possible, be kept in isolation, provided with necessary medicines and nutritious food, and cared for under proper hygiene.
Experts said it takes several weeks after vaccination for the body to develop adequate immunity. Therefore, alongside vaccination, rapid case detection, isolation of infected children and timely treatment remain equally important.
Bangladesh introduced the Measles-Rubella (MR) vaccine under its national immunization programme in 2012. Following a nationwide MR campaign in 2014, infections declined significantly. Although vaccine coverage reached nearly 90% in 2018 and 2019, routine immunization was disrupted during the Covid-19 pandemic, causing many children to miss scheduled vaccinations. Public health experts say the effects of those gaps are now becoming evident on a large scale.
Professor Mahmudur Rahman, chairman of the National Immunization Technical Advisory Group (NITAG), said infections have not declined as quickly as expected since the vaccination campaign ended.
"It is now important to analyse detailed data to determine which age groups are being affected the most. The next strategy can be developed based on those findings," he said.
To contain the outbreak, the government first launched a special MR vaccination campaign in 30 high-risk upazilas and later in four city corporations. It then carried out a nationwide campaign from April 20 to May 20. The DGHS says the campaign vaccinated more children than initially targeted. Health workers are now identifying children who missed vaccination and administering vaccines through door-to-door visits.
DGHS Director General Professor Dr Prabhat Chandra Biswas said there are currently no confirmed measles deaths, but efforts to vaccinate unvaccinated children are continuing.
"We hope that just as confirmed measles deaths have fallen to zero, suspected measles deaths will also gradually decline to zero. To achieve that, we are identifying children who missed vaccination, ensuring they receive vaccines, strengthening disease surveillance and improving treatment services," he said.

item.title: Acting speaker calls for building discrimination-free Bangladesh against imperialism, hegemony
item.description:
Acting Speaker of the National Parliament Barrister Kayser Kamal, MP, on Wednesday called for building a discrimination-free Bangladesh free from imperialism and hegemony, urging all to remain steadfast in upholding the spirit of the July Mass Uprising.
"While fighting against fascism, those who embraced martyrdom and those who were injured deserve our deepest respect. We remember them with profound reverence on the anniversary of the Borsha Biplab (Monsoon Revolution)," he said.
The acting speaker made the remarks while addressing a cultural program titled "Songs of the Monsoon Revolution" as the chief guest at Manik Mia Avenue in the capital, organized marking the Victory Day of the July Mass Uprising.
He said the nation must remain firmly committed to building a discrimination-free Bangladesh free from imperialism and hegemonic influence, said a press release of parliament secretariat.
Chief Whip of the National Parliament Md Nurul Islam, MP, Opposition Chief Whip Md Nahid Islam, MP, and Whip ABM Ashraf Uddin Nizan, MP, attended the programme as special guests.
Speaking on the occasion, Chief Whip Md Nurul Islam said the nation must not deviate from the ideals of the victory achieved through the uprising.
"We must ensure that the dreams of the young generation are never trampled upon again," he said, adding that the spirit of the Monsoon Revolution should be cherished in the hearts of the people.
Whip ABM Ashraf Uddin Nizan said the nation must remain united in the face of any national crisis and stay vigilant to prevent the rise of fascism in the future.
Opposition Chief Whip Md Nahid Islam said the struggle for building a discrimination-free Bangladesh must continue. He also paid deep tribute to the martyrs of the July uprising.
Leaders of the NCP, including its Convener and Member of Parliament Hasnat Abdullah, also addressed the program, expressing their firm commitment to building a transformed Bangladesh above all differences and divisions.

item.title: Board-less Islami Bank struggles amid Tk1,316cr loss in H1’26
item.description:
Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC, long considered the bedrock of Bangladesh’s Islamic banking industry and owner of the country's largest private deposit base, is facing an unprecedented governance and operational crisis.
For over a month and a half, the systemically important bank has been operating without a chairman, a functional board of directors, or a regular managing director.
Following severe governance breakdowns, controversial loan disbursements, and intense liquidity pressure, Bangladesh Bank dissolved the entire board on June 14, 2026, appointing executive director Mohammad Zahir Hossain as administrator.
While routine retail counters remain open, corporate clients, importers, and industrial borrowers report severe decision-making bottlenecks across large credit approvals, Letters of Credit (LCs), and working capital lines.
The bank reported a consolidated net loss of Tk1,316.48 crore for the first half of 2026 (H1), compared to a net profit of Tk67.40 crore in H1 2025—a negative shift of Tk1,383.88 crore in twelve months.
Operating losses reached Tk1,016 crore in Q2 alone (up from Tk 274 crore in Q1), bringing total H1 operating losses to Tk1,285 crore.
Total deposits plummeted by Tk21,365 crore in a single quarter, falling from Tk185,698 crore in March 2026 to Tk164,333 crore by late June.
Total assets stand at Tk240,955 crore against outstanding loans of Tk188,633 crore.
Market sources indicate that nearly half of the total loan portfolio faces default risks, largely linked to ~Tk80,000 crore in contested exposures associated with the S Alam Group.
To avert a systemic payment collapse, Bangladesh Bank injected approximately Tk17,000 crore in emergency liquidity support prior to appointing the Administrator.
Corporate friction & credit bottlenecks
Although day-to-day retail transactions have stabilized, the absence of a board and executive leadership has stalled major corporate financing decisions.
Industrial borrowers, particularly in the Readymade Garment (RMG) sector, report that delayed working capital renewals and LC openings are disrupting raw material imports, worker payrolls, and export delivery schedules.
The bank's current administration maintains that panic has subsided, fresh deposits are returning, and dependency on central bank liquidity support is decreasing.
According to administrator Mohammad Zahir Hossain, rational business proposals are being processed, though speculative or high-risk financing requests are being turned down.
Acting managing director Md Altaf Hossain noted that while corporate deposit collection remains challenging, core operational stability is being preserved.
"Operating a systemically important bank under an Administrator can only be a temporary stopgap measure," observed Prof Mustafizur Rahman, distinguished fellow at the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD).
"For an institution carrying nearly three crore deposit accounts, vast corporate portfolios, and extensive trade finance obligations, prolonged leadership uncertainty erodes market trust. Bangladesh Bank must urgently reconstitute a professional, highly credible board of directors and appoint a regular managing director to restore corporate confidence and streamline credit operations."
Banking analysts emphasize that Islami Bank’s crisis serves as a major test of regulatory oversight and corporate governance in Bangladesh's financial sector.
Unwinding decade-long governance weaknesses, recovering non-performing assets, and restoring the bank's financial health will require a fully empowered, transparent board working alongside strict regulatory supervision.
While administrative intervention prevented an immediate run on the bank, managing daily operations through an Administrator is unsustainable for Bangladesh's largest private lender.
The prompt reconstitution of a qualified, independent board of directors remains essential to restoring public confidence, unlocking industrial credit, and stabilizing the broader banking sector.
